claims.claim: Law 171-07 exempts the income declared by rentistas and pensionados

sources.name: Pellerano & Herrera: Pensionado or rentista under Law 171-07
sources.says: Dated 2 April 2010 (law of 2007). "Las rentas o sumas declaradas como ingreso por los beneficiarios de esta ley estarán exentas" of income tax; rentista: "una suma mensual correspondiente a USD$2,000.00" of stable income mainly from abroad, including deposits or investments in foreign banks, investments in companies abroad and interest on foreign-currency securities; pensionado: "no menor de USD$1,500.00" plus "USD$250.00" per dependant. Investor residence is a separate programme; no amount given.

claims.note: Read on a law firm's 2010 summary of the 2007 law; a search for a 2026 amendment of Law 171-07 found none. Also the summary and why line.

claims.claim: There is no US estate treaty

sources.name: IRS: Estate & gift tax treaties (international)
sources.says: The table has 15 countries (see us-estate-treaty-list); none of the 37 countries named in this claim is among them.

claims.claim: So there would be no US credit for it on US-sited stocks

sources.name: Cornell LII: 26 U.S. Code § 2014, credit for foreign death taxes
sources.says: Subsection (a): the estate tax is credited with foreign estate, inheritance, legacy or succession taxes "actually paid to any foreign country in respect of any property situated within such foreign country".

claims.note: Without a treaty the statutory credit reaches only property sited in the DR, so a DR tax on US-sited stocks gets no US credit.
